六级大纲词汇 · 04英文原文

Dinner by the Courtyard Grill

院子里的晚餐 · 594 词 · 7 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1The bakery smelled of garlic, mint, and pastry. Mei, an amiable cook, was preparing a feast of local cuisine to open a community kitchen. Guests craved the kitchen's grilled salmon, crisp vegetables, and pumpkin pudding. On the porch stood a bouquet and an assortment of bowls. Inside, her apprentice stacked cartons beside a tub of dough and a pot of porridge. Then a fault cut power to the block. Mei checked the refrigerator, put the ingredients that were still cold on ice, and crossed her elaborate menu off the board.

2A brewery next door offered a courtyard grill. Mei could keep the salmon if its temperature remained safe. Several quarts of batter and creamy dressing were harder to manage. The sight of so much food might tempt anyone to use it before it spoiled. Instead, she set them aside and looked at yesterday's bread. She broke a chunk in her apron and heard the crust crunch. If she toasted it on the grill, stale bread could become the base of a dish her guests could eat from bowls.

3They made a stew from the vegetables intended for assorted side dishes. The apprentice peeled limes while Mei put cauliflower, pumpkin, and olives into a pot. Crumbled bread replaced the carbohydrate they had planned to serve as pasta. A sheet of foil slipped from a tray. Mei secured its rim under a heavy porcelain plate. Two volunteers scrubbed the grill with detergent and scraped grease from a pan. They moved bleach well away from the cooking area and fetched clean linen for the tables.

4A waiter offered to brew coffee and open some complimentary ale. She kept the coffee for later. Mint and lime water would make a sober alternative to cocktails. The fragrant jug drew a passerby to the gate. He had come from a stall where someone was peddling sweets. Mei invited him to lay out bowls. He returned with spoons. The fragrance of mint had been his temptation. Soon the people waiting began to mingle in the courtyard.

5Mei lifted the lid on the spicy broth. She had added too much spice. The spice drowned out the vegetables' flavor, though their texture was good. The apprentice skimmed off the foam and folded in plain beans left over from a spaghetti sauce. Then he wanted to flip the fish before it released from the greasy grill. Mei showed him where one side had turned crisp. She saved a ration for the electrician, who wanted to know how much sodium it contained. At the same time the waiter took a cork from a bottle of vinegar so diners could season their own bowls.

6There was no oven for pudding, so they served coconut jelly from the shop and sprinkled toasted crumbs on top. It was a small indulgence after a wholesome meal. A jolly guest called it a fabulous delicacy. The apprentice wanted to indulge guests with extravagant pastry. Even an indulgent guest might like this simpler specialty. After a hectic evening, he could still remember what had gone in each pot.

7When the power returned, Mei left the oven off. Neighbors had made the courtyard cozy with chairs borrowed from both sides of the street. The apprentice took a card from a stationery box and wrote out the recipe. He used a stapler to fasten it to the pantry door. Mei wrote underneath, "Keep a dish you can cook without electricity." It was cheaper than the opening extravagance they had planned, and it would be there the next time someone turned the lights off.

六级大纲词汇 · 04中文译文

院子里的晚餐

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1面包房里飘着大蒜、薄荷和点心的香气。和气的厨师梅正为社区厨房的开张准备一桌当地风味的菜。客人盼着吃到烤三文鱼、爽脆的蔬菜和南瓜布丁。门廊上放着一束花和各式各样的碗。屋里，学徒在一桶面团和一锅粥旁码放纸盒。这时，一场故障让整个街区停了电。梅检查冰箱，把温度仍然够低的食材放到冰上，然后从黑板上划掉了那份精心设计的菜单。

2隔壁的啤酒厂愿意借出院子里的烤架。只要温度保持安全，三文鱼就还能用。几夸脱面糊和奶油酱却难处理。望着这么多食物，谁都会想趁它们变质前用掉。梅先把它们放到一边，转头看见昨天剩下的面包。她掰下一块，面包皮咔嚓一声，碎屑落在围裙上。把面包放在烤架上烘一烘，隔夜面包就能做成一道用碗盛的菜。

3他们把原本要做成各式配菜的蔬菜炖在一起。学徒剥青柠时，梅往锅里放进花椰菜、南瓜和橄榄。掰碎的面包代替了原先打算用意面提供的碳水化合物。一张锡纸从托盘上滑落。梅用沉重的瓷盘压住边缘。两名志愿者用清洁剂刷烤架，把锅里的油脂刮掉。他们把漂白剂移到远离烹饪区的地方，又拿了干净的亚麻布铺桌。

4一位服务员提议煮咖啡，再开些免费的麦芽啤酒。梅把咖啡留到稍后，先用薄荷青柠水招待想喝无酒精饮品的人。壶里的香气把一个路人引到门口。他刚从卖糖果的小摊过来。梅请他帮忙摆碗。他拿着勺子回来，说自己就是被薄荷香勾过来的。很快，等候的人开始在院子里聊起来。

5梅掀开汤锅的盖子。她的香料放多了。蔬菜的口感虽好，味道却被盖住了。学徒撇去浮沫，拌进了做意面酱剩下的白水煮豆。鱼还粘在油乎乎的烤架上，他就想翻面。梅指给他看哪一侧已经烤脆了。她给电工留了一份，他想知道里面有多少钠。与此同时，服务员拔开一瓶醋的软木塞，让食客自己给碗里的菜调味。

6烤不了布丁，他们就用店里买来的椰子冻撒上烤面包屑。一顿实在的饭后，吃点甜品也算小小的享受。一位乐呵呵的客人说那真是道美味。学徒本来想用豪华的点心款待大家，后来发现，哪怕平时爱吃好东西的客人，也会喜欢这道简单的特色菜。忙了一晚，他仍然记得每个锅里都放过什么。

7电恢复了，梅没有开烤箱。街坊从街道两边搬来椅子，把院子布置得暖融融的。学徒从文具盒里找出卡片，把食谱写上去，再用订书机钉在储藏室门上。梅添了一行字，留一道不用电也能做的菜。这比原来打算铺张办的开张宴省钱，而且下次灯再灭时，他们还有一份能照着做的食谱。
